title: The motions of the will in prevenient grace arise naturally
source_text: XCV. Motus vero voluntatis, in quibus gratia praeveniens consistit, ex illius mente, sunt certi quidam affectus, quibus praevia cognitione, voluntas erigitur, & invitatur, tum ad eliciendam spem, tum ad diligendum Deum, aut dolendum de peccatis, antequam actum spei, aut amoris, vel doloris ex dilectione ejus eliciat. Ad hujusmodi vero motus & affectus non cooperatur voluntas, qua liberum arbitrium est, sed solum qua voluntas, & natura quaedam est. Quippe velit nolit, praesente cognitione, naturaliter in ea insurgunt. Rationem autem gratiae non habent, nisi Deus simul in eosdem specialiter influat, ut evadant supernaturales, & certo quoque modo ad salutem accommodentur.
pass_a_gloss: XCV. But the motions of the will, in which prevenient grace consists, according to his mind, are certain affections, by which, cognition going before, the will is raised, & invited, both to eliciting hope, and to loving God, or grieving for sins, before it elicits the act of hope, or of love, or of grief from love of him. But to motions & affections of this kind the will does not cooperate, as it is free choice, but only as it is will, & a certain nature. Since whether it will or not, cognition being present, they rise up naturally in it. But they do not have the character of grace, unless God at the same time flows specially into them, that they become supernatural, & also in a certain manner be accommodated to salvation.
pass_b_english: Thesis XCV. On his view the motions of the will that make up prevenient grace are certain affections. Once knowledge has gone before, they raise and invite the will to elicit hope, to love God or to grieve for sins, before it elicits the act of hope, or of love, or of grief arising from love of him.

The will does not cooperate in these motions and affections as free choice, but only as will, that is, as a kind of nature. Whether it wants them or not, they rise up in it naturally once the knowledge is present. They have the character of grace only if God at the same time flows specially into them, so that they become supernatural and are also fitted in a certain way for salvation.

lemmas.latin: qua liberum arbitrium est, sed solum qua voluntas
lemmas.gloss: as it is free choice, but only as it is will

lemmas.latin: nisi Deus simul in eosdem specialiter influat
lemmas.gloss: unless God at the same time flows specially into them

choices.why: Molina's pre-volitional motions of the will toward a known good, arising naturally, not freely.

bible_refs: Luis de Molina SJ, Concordia liberi arbitrii cum gratiae donis (Lisbon, 1588), question 14, article 13, disputation 45.
